doc.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Practice habits
summary: He quotes a Van Eps saying about practice and describes his routine.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Right. I read a little quote that you had said, I think it’s you, about practicing. And if you don’t practice for one day, that you notice it? How did that go?

Oh, right. I was paraphrasing someone else. I think it dates back to one of the great classical musicians or something. I heard it from George Van Eps, via George Van Eps. Yeah, if I don’t practice for one day I notice it; if I don’t practice for two days, the conductor notices it; and if I don’t practice it for three days everybody notices.
Yeah. What’s your practice — if you sit to practice, what do you practice these days?

Well I try to practice things that cover all the technical moves and I try to practice things that involve, again, musical contexts that I like. I try to play some things that have a lot of single notes, like some Bach preludes or something like that, and I try to practice some © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
chordal things, I try to play some tunes, and explore some new tunes that I’m learning, and a little bit of stuff like that basically. Not enough of course.
